content.text:
You are a TLA+ specification engineer. You will receive a natural language description of a system. Produce a complete, syntactically correct TLA+ specification that faithfully captures the described behavior. The output must be a valid TLA+ module that passes the SANY parser. Include the MODULE declaration, EXTENDS, CONSTANTS, VARIABLES, Init, Next and Spec. Include all safety invariants and liveness properties described, and any fairness conditions mentioned. Output only the TLA+ specification.

System description: The `OldPlusCal` module is a utility/specification module that formalizes the translation from a +CAL algorithm's abstract syntax tree (AST) to its TLA+ description. It is not a model of a running system but rather a functional specification of the +CAL-to-TLA+ compiler's core translation logic, intended to be partially executable by TLC.

The module defines the grammar of +CAL ASTs through predicates and set definitions covering all syntactic constructs: algorithms (uniprocess and multiprocess), procedures, processes, variable declarations, labeled statements, while loops, label sequences, simple statements (assignment, if, either, with, when, print, assert, skip), call/return/callReturn, and goto. TLA+ expressions are represented throughout as sequences of string lexemes.

The central operator `Translation(alg, fairnessOption)` takes a well-formed algorithm AST and a fairness option (empty string, `"wf"`, `"wfNext"`, or `"sf"`) and produces a sequence of lexemes constituting the corresponding TLA+ specification. This involves: exploding labeled statements into simple atomic-action definitions via `FullyExplodeSeq` and `Explode`; translating procedure calls, returns, and gotos into explicit assignments to `pc` and `stack`; adding subscripts to local variables for multiprocess algorithms; generating the `Init`, `Next`, `Spec`, `ProcSet`, `vars`, and `Termination` definitions; and optionally appending weak or strong fairness conditions. The module concludes with an `ASSUME` that, when TLC is run, computes and prints `Translation(ast, fairness)` for externally supplied `ast` and `fairness` constants.
